record.paper_title: A collection of open problems in celebration of Imre Leader’s 60th birthday
record.original_question: Does there exist an absolute constant c > 0 such that for every n ≥ 4, the maximum size g_{P_3}(n) of a family of graphs on [n] in which any two graphs intersect in a copy of the 3-edge path P_3 satisfies g_{P_3}(n) ≤ (1 - c) 2^{(n choose 2) - 1}?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.5 (Alon, Spencer). There exists an absolute constant c > 0 such that gP3(n) ≤ (1 − c)2^((n choose 2)−1) for all n ≥ 4.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \ge 4$ be an integer and identify the vertex set $[n] = \{1,2,\dots,n\}$. A graph on $[n]$ is a subset of the edge set $\binom{[n]}{2}$; there are $2^{\binom{n}{2}}$ such graphs. Let $P_3$ denote the path with $3$ edges (equivalently, the path on $4$ vertices). A family $\mathcal{F}$ of graphs on $[n]$ is called $P_3$-intersecting if for every pair of graphs $G_1, G_2 \in \mathcal{F}$, the edge-intersection $E(G_1) \cap E(G_2)$ contains a copy of $P_3$. Define
$$g_{P_3}(n) = \max\{|\mathcal{F}| : \mathcal{F} \text{ is a } P_3\text{-intersecting family of graphs on } [n]\}.$$
Note the trivial upper bound $g_{P_3}(n) \le 2^{\binom{n}{2}-1}$ (since for any fixed edge $e$ contained in some $P_3$, at most half of all graphs can contain $e$).

Does there exist an absolute constant $c > 0$ such that
$$g_{P_3}(n) \;\le\; (1-c)\, 2^{\binom{n}{2}-1} \qquad \text{for all } n \ge 4 ?$$
artifact.status_search_result: A recent preprint (Hamrick–Hu, 2025) on lower bounds for intersection families of graphs explicitly references the Alon–Spencer conjecture on $g_{P_3}(n)$ and provides constructions / partial bounds but does not resolve it. No source found claiming a proof or disproof, so the conjecture appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Lower Bounds on Intersection Families for Certain Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: References Alon–Spencer work on intersecting families of graphs and provides bounds/constructions for P_3-intersecting families without resolving the conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The Alon–Spencer conjecture g_{P_3}(n) ≤ (1−c) 2^{C(n,2)−1} is discussed but not proven or disproven in this 2025 work.
